notes.body:
# Theme: Manual Appendix ABC Data Management

## Definition
Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual, ongoing consolidation of a high-volume device portfolio from fragmented internal sources. Excel cannot reliably support the reuse and update work required.

## Associated Codes
- #code/versioned-excel-master-data
- #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance
- #code/high-volume-product-data
- #code/fragmented-product-data-sources
- #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel
- #code/misaligned-appendix-structures
- #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions
- #code/cross-tab-data-navigation
- #code/restricted-row-editing
- #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation

## Representative Quotes
> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated." - P01

> "We find some trouble in copy and paste the data from one to another file, not always being possible to edit the Excel." - P01

> "Nicht mal Appendix ABC von MDSAP und MDAR sind angeglichen." - P02
>
> Translation: "Not even Appendix ABC for MDSAP and MDR are aligned."

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel, weil ich brauche es ja eh, die Revision 09 vom MDR Appendix, weil der MDSAP Appendix brauch ich parallel jedes Jahr, weil der hat noch die ganzen Ablaufdaten hinten drin." - P02
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel because I need revision 09 of the MDR Appendix anyway; I also need the MDSAP Appendix in parallel every year because it still contains all the expiry dates."

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "We have to fill in again all the information for all products." - P03

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch." - P04
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."

> "Das Hin und Hergeklicke, das stimmt." - P04
>
> Translation: "All the clicking back and forth, that is true."

> "So now we're having to go back through now and do a complete assessment of the 10,000 CFNs and ensure that you know everything is accurate." - P05

> "The one that comes to mind most prominently is probably Appendix C for the suppliers." - P05

> "Das ist beim TÜV Süd auch 'ne Excel-Liste, wo halt aus meiner Sicht 'ne Tabellenkalkulationssoftware verwendet wurde, um 'ne Datenbank aufzubauen. Ist aus meiner Richtung nicht gut geeignet." - P06
>
> Translation: "At TUV SUD it is also an Excel list where, from my perspective, a spreadsheet application is being used to build a database. From my perspective, it is not well suited."

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam." - P06
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen." - P07
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind." - P07
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio." - P08
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."

> "Komplex machen es erstmal die ganz vielen Arbeitsmappen, das ist schon mal komplex, die unterschiedlichsten Informationen, die quasi seitens der benannten Stelle aus unserer Sicht erforderlich sind." - P08
>
> Translation: "What makes it complex first of all are the many worksheets and the very different kinds of information that, from our perspective, the notified body requires."

> "Wenn dann sich mal was in der Produktfamilie zum Beispiel in A. 3 ändert, dann denkt man vielleicht nicht dran, nach vorne zu springen. Es ist menschlich." - P08
>
> Translation: "If something changes in the product family, for example in A.3, people may not think to jump back to the front. It is human."

> "Also zum einen ist es, es sind es die Funktionen in der Excel-Liste, die limitiert sind, wenn man an mehrere 1000 Artikelnummern kommt." - P09
>
> Translation: "The functions in the Excel list are limited when you reach several thousand article numbers."

> "Wenn sich ein Zertifikat ändert, muss der Datensatz viermal angepasst werden, wo wurde vielleicht in einer Liste nicht angepasst, wurde vergessen, dann haben wir 2 Wahrheiten, welches Zertifikat gilt jetzt, das hat auch schon zu vielen Fragen geführt." - P09
>
> Translation: "When a certificate changes, the record has to be adjusted four times; perhaps one list was not updated or was forgotten, and then we have two versions of the truth about which certificate applies, which has already led to many questions."

> "Das, das, das, das meiste ist, glaube ich, dass man alles wieder neu eintragen muss, ja, weil sich ja gefühlt alle drei Wochen die Version oder Revision." - P10
>
> Translation: "The main issue is that you have to enter everything again because it feels as though the version or revision changes every three weeks."

> "Man muss eigentlich jede Zeile, jede Spalte, jede Zelle angucken, was man da jetzt wirklich eintragen muss." - P10
>
> Translation: "You essentially have to look at every row, every column, and every cell to determine what must be entered."

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen." - P11
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

> "Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer." - P11
>
> Translation: "The main pain points at present are that we have to maintain three appendices, in whatever form."

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 considers Appendix ABC important as a summary of device technical specifications; P02 values a living version that supports coordination; P03 says a small, certificate-specific site list could remain separate; P04 uses it as a required certification artifact but not as the primary working basis for discussions. P05 sees the metadata itself as manageable but identifies supplier and high-volume maintenance as especially vulnerable to source-to-source errors. P06 values the data purpose but reports that the spreadsheet becomes slow at scale. P07 needs the data for certification but reports manual maintenance across multiple certificate-specific files and fragile links among A, B, and C. P08 sees the data as necessary but reports many worksheets, multiple source systems, and cross-tab dependencies. P09 says the agreed TUV-managed template migration minimizes customer migration effort, but it temporarily blocks editors and does not remove duplicate maintenance across certificate-specific lists. P10 needs the data but reports that frequent revisions and misaligned MDR/MDD structures require row-by-row, cell-by-cell re-entry. P11 says a TUV-provided migration can help, but still copies one update into each related project and general repository. The problem is the manual, duplicated maintenance burden, not the purpose of the data.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains High: P11 provides an eleventh direct confirmation and specifies project-by-project duplication, naming, and upload work on top of maintaining three Appendix variants. Test which supplier certificate and site fields can be sourced or verified automatically and which authorized record edits require audit controls.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[High-Effort Appendix ABC Maintenance]]
- [[Restricted Appendix Rows Force Parallel Reference Lists]]

## Linked Insights
- [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]]
- [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]]

notes.body:
# Theme: Scalable Structured Data Collaboration

## Definition
A future digital workflow must accept data at the project stage where it is known, support bulk reuse for large portfolios, and retain a cross-portfolio overview for customer and reviewer collaboration.

## Associated Codes
- #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow
- #code/bulk-data-entry-needed
- #code/portfolio-level-data-overview
- #code/development-data-evolves
- #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity
- #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data
- #code/system-to-system-data-integration
- #code/eudamed-data-reuse
- #code/automated-data-validity-checks
- #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates
- #code/certification-process-performance-metrics
- #code/role-based-data-governance
- #code/shared-data-audit-trail
- #code/exemplar-submission-disconnected-from-change-scope
- #code/editable-structured-records

## Representative Quotes
> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information." - P01

> "In parallel way will be very useful to have also the system that if this information can put in a table or Excel file in order to see also the same view of appendix ABC of today." - P01

> "Für mich reicht eigentlich, wenn es so ist, theoretisch bei Udemed. Und von dem her, es muss keine Machine to Machine sein. Ich denke, mit Excel hochladen ist für uns vollkommen in Ordnung." - P02
>
> Translation: "For me, it is enough if it is theoretically like EUDAMED. It does not have to be machine-to-machine. I think uploading Excel is completely fine for us."

> "Was ist, wenn sich was ändert? Ich denk, das ist das größte Thema von allem. Wie merk ich das?" - P02
>
> Translation: "What happens when something changes? I think that is the biggest issue of all. How do I notice it?"

> "The solution of machine system that speak together will be the best solution." - P03

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information." - P03

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export." - P04
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."

> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion." - P04
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."

> "We have that metadata within, you know, our own systems." - P05

> "We always welcome more metrics, so I think that would be extremely helpful for us as we're not only planning projects, but that also kind of take a look internally on what can we do if we need to resource." - P05

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden." - P06
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."

> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht." - P07
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise." - P08
>
> Translation: "We cannot simply press a button and tell it to take the data from a particular database on our side and put it into the table in a particular way."

> "Dann kommt es ganz oft mit Hashtag Wert Ausrufezeichen und wir wissen halt auch nicht, was haben wir jetzt da falsch gemacht oder ist da jetzt, also es verunsichert halt einfach 'n bisschen." - P08
>
> Translation: "It often then shows hashtag value exclamation mark, and we do not know what we have done wrong; it is simply a bit unsettling."

> "Also ich würd es, glaub ich, nicht begrüßen, wenn sie eigenständig ändern. Also ich glaub, es sollte schon irgendwie immer in Rücksprache mit uns erfolgen." - P08
>
> Translation: "I do not think I would welcome it if you changed things independently. I think it should always happen in consultation with us."

> "Das ist natürlich auch unser Wunsch, dass man 'ne Situation hat, wo man bei uns in der in der Datenbank 'ne Information einträgt und der Datensatz, wenn er dann komplett ist, halt auch transferiert werden kann, so wie das für die Eutermed auch funktioniert, dass man da nichts händisch eintragen muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "Our wish is to enter information in our database and transfer the record once it is complete, as with EUDAMED, so that nothing has to be entered manually."

> "Dann vielleicht auch mit dem Status 'ne klare Abgrenzung, was dürfen wir umsetzen, also welchen Status dürfen wir ändern und welchen Status dürfen wir nicht setzen, also dass wir gar nicht die Möglichkeit haben, vielleicht was auf Covered by Certificate oder Ähnlichem zu setzen, weil das 'ne reine TÜV-Offline wäre." - P09
>
> Translation: "Statuses should clearly distinguish what we may change and what we may not set, so that we cannot set something to 'Covered by Certificate' because that would be solely for TUV."

> "Wir müssen aber immer im Hinterkopf behalten, wir haben da noch 100 andere Artikel, die auch über diesen selben Vorgang laufen, die haben wir aber nicht eingereicht, die müssen aber dann im Nachgang auch alle noch gepflegt werden." - P09
>
> Translation: "We must always remember that another 100 articles run through the same change; we did not submit them, but they all still have to be maintained afterward."

> "Also nachvollziehbar über 'ne Änderungshistorie wäre wichtig, dass man letzten Endes sieht, was ist an dem Datensatz aktuell geändert worden oder was ist in der Änderung und mit welchem Bezug zu einem zu welchem Projekt ist das gerade in der Änderung?" - P09
>
> Translation: "A traceable change history would be important so that one can see what has been changed in the record, what is currently being changed, and which project the change relates to."

> "Wenn jetzt die Schnittstelle ein Standardformat ist, das wäre natürlich sehr gut." - P10
>
> Translation: "If the interface used a standard format, that would naturally be very good."

> "Wie gesagt, so gut es geht digital zu haben, kein PDF mehr ausdrucken zu müssen, um irgendwas reinzugeben und dann ist digital zu unterschreiben, wie auch immer das da der Austausch da ist." - P10
>
> Translation: "As far as possible, it should be digital: no more printing PDFs to enter something and then signing digitally."

> "Dass man da in gewisser Art und Weise und ich weiß, ihr habt dann betrifft darf ja dann auch nicht beraten, aber gibt es dann so eine Art Vorprüfung oder sonst irgendwas? Geht es in die Richtung, wo ich mir wünschen würde, als Kunde vielleicht dazu sagen, ich schicke das einfach mal zum Check ein und es läuft durch und gibt mir dann die formalen Punkte." - P10
>
> Translation: "Could there be some kind of preliminary check? I would like to submit something for a check and have it identify the formal issues."

> "Wenn wir das itembasiert oder produktbasiert updaten konnten, das ware, glaube ich, schon mal unheimlich hilfreich." - P11
>
> Translation: "If we could update it by item or product, that would be extremely helpful."

> "Also automatisierte Anpassungen wurde ich gerne ausschliessen. Wenn dann mit Frage." - P11
>
> Translation: "I would like to exclude automated changes. If anything, they should happen with a question."

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 considers some initial project information easy to provide, but says supplier and manufacturing information can be premature for early-stage or phased submissions. P02 prefers Excel upload over a machine-to-machine interface, while P03 and P04 identify system-to-system exchange as ideal and template upload as a practical compromise. P05 needs a system that can coexist with internal metadata sources and expose planning metrics. P06 has mature product data but needs a mixture of EUDAMED reuse, other-source enrichment, and guided input. P07 requires a controllable interface from multiple internal systems and distinct contributor, reviewer, and approver rights. P08 wants data transfer from manufacturer systems, but validation that warns rather than independently overwrites manufacturer data. P09 wants system-to-system transfer but acknowledges that some source data still live in documents and that transfer timing must follow internal change control. P10 wants a standardized interface and automated formal pre-checks, but confirms that its current data sources remain distributed. P11 confirms that source changes must wait for regulatory approval and that automation should propose, not silently apply, consequential updates. An API is valuable when the customer has a sufficiently structured leading system, not a universal prerequisite.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains High: P11 adds an eleventh direct confirmation and makes approval-gated synchronization plus user-confirmed automation explicit controls. Test which integrations, imports, certificate lookups, guided workflows, and reports can preserve data ownership and auditability.

## Linked Pain Points
No current-state pain point is linked yet; this is a future-state requirement theme.

## Linked Insights
- [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]]
- [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]]

Wie gesagt, so gut es geht digital zu haben, kein PDF mehr ausdrucken zu müssen, um irgendwas reinzugeben und dann ist digital zu unterschreiben, wie auch immer das da der Austausch da ist.

Dass man da in gewisser Art und Weise und ich weiß, ihr habt dann betrifft darf ja dann auch nicht beraten, aber gibt es dann so eine Art Vorprüfung oder sonst irgendwas? Geht es in die Richtung, wo ich mir wünschen würde, als Kunde vielleicht dazu sagen, ich schicke das einfach mal zum Check ein und es läuft durch und gibt mir dann die formalen Punkte.
Wenn wir das itembasiert oder produktbasiert updaten konnten, das ware, glaube ich, schon mal unheimlich hilfreich.
Also automatisierte Anpassungen wurde ich gerne ausschliessen. Wenn dann mit Frage.

# Theme: Unclear Commercial Closure and Support

## Definition
After technical work concludes, unclear service completion, invoice timing, and occasional unavailable support make financial and administrative closure difficult.

## Associated Codes
- #code/unclear-billing-closure
- #code/unanswered-process-support

## Representative Quotes
> "It's not clear for me when the process ends with the service cost invoice payment." - P01

> "There are some delay in our invoice, and then our department, the account department is sometimes very in trouble for close relativity and all that." - P01

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 has named contacts for technical matters; the reported support gap concerns obtaining answers about this information, not the absence of every relationship.

## Related Evidence
P02 reports unclear pre-quotation costs and assessment-module rationale. This is related commercial evidence but concerns commercial scoping before service acceptance, rather than closure or support; interview count and confidence are unchanged.

## Open Questions
Are late invoices an isolated operational issue or a predictable consequence of unclear completion criteria?

## Linked Pain Points
- [[Unclear Invoice Timing Delays Administrative Closure]]

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: only one interview supports this preliminary theme.

notes.body:
# Theme: Unpredictable Commercial Scoping

## Definition
Before a quotation is accepted, the customer cannot reliably understand review-cost components or why assessment modules are included. The uncertain scope makes budget estimation and challenge of the proposed assessment difficult.

## Associated Codes
- #code/opaque-review-costs
- #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale

## Representative Quotes
> "Und dort wissen wir ganz genau, was ein Experte kostet und wie viel nachher der Experte für einen Review abgerechnet hat." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we know exactly what an expert costs and how much the expert charged for a review."

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?" - P07
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

## Contradicting Evidence
P02 understands which certification service to request; the uncertainty concerns cost and assessment-module scope, not basic service selection. P07 also needs routine-cost estimates but reports that explanations arrive only after repeated follow-up.

## Related Evidence
P09 reports that additional technical-documentation requests can emerge during assessment and that change types require repeated clarification about documents and modules. This is adjacent to scope predictability, but it does not directly confirm missing pre-quotation cost or module rationale, so interview and quote counts are unchanged.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains Medium: P07 provides a second direct cross-company confirmation that costs can arrive without sufficient rationale for budget planning. Test which explanation, cost breakdown, and forecast would be sufficient for customers to predict and challenge scope before quotation acceptance.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[Opaque Cost and Assessment Scope]]

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: two interviews directly support this theme, but it has not connected strongly enough to a second theme to justify an insight.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Pain Point Register

Last consolidated: 2026-07-30. All sixteen pain points were reviewed after P09. PP13 concerns action-required alerts that can be missed, while PP15 concerns subscriptions that cannot be scoped independently from access, so the underlying mechanisms remain distinct. PP14 concerns document continuity after project creation, while PP16 concerns the missing immutable timestamp before project creation.

P10 update: PP17 concerns customer-led request initiation before a project exists, PP18 concerns acknowledging an already-seen notification, and PP19 concerns completing a locked signed form. These mechanisms are distinct from PP07 request follow-up, PP13 missed action alerts, and existing document-continuity pains. P11 directly confirms PP01, PP02, and PP19; no new pain point is required because project-specific Appendix copying, open-draft reconciliation, and locked quotation rework match their existing underlying mechanisms. # Pain Point: Change Assessment Lags Internal Change Progress

**Theme:** [[Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change]]
**Description:** Internal work continues while a submitted change awaits notified-body approval, so later changes may no longer match the submitted documentation.
**Trigger:** A change assessment has a long interval between submission and approval.
**Impact:** Implementation may be postponed, documentation becomes stale, and the company may need to use expedited assessment.
**Workaround:** Plan changes earlier and use monthly meetings or an expedited process when timing becomes critical.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on." - P03

> "We try to plan as much as possible all the changes, but sometimes it's not possible and we need to use the expedite process." - P03

## Possible Opportunity
Test shared assessment states, expected approval dates, and a mechanism to flag related internal changes before the submitted package becomes outdated.

# Pain Point: Critical UCI Notifications Can Be Missed

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** Deficiency questions can arrive in UCI without a reliable accompanying personal email, and high notification volume can cause the system alert to be overlooked.
**Trigger:** A reviewer issues a deficiency or question through UCI.
**Impact:** The manufacturer can discover action-required questions one to two weeks late, delaying its response and the review.
**Workaround:** Wait for personal email and periodically check UCI manually.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P05

**Representative Quotes:**
> "There's been instances where like we've received deficiencies, but we're kind of old school, I guess, and so we wait for the e-mail." - P05

> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

## Possible Opportunity
Test a configurable, high-salience alert for action-required deficiencies, with clear acknowledgement and escalation states rather than increasing general notification volume.

## Related Evidence
P09 reports receiving about 20 irrelevant notifications per week because administrator access automatically brings broad notification coverage. This supports the risk that high volume can hide important alerts, but P09 does not report a missed action-required message, so evidence and interview counts are unchanged.

# Pain Point: Customer Change IDs Disappear Across TUV Process

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** The participant's change-notification ID is not retained in TUV correspondence, feedback, or invoices after the request receives a TUV project ID.
**Trigger:** Following a submitted change across TUV feedback, project communication, and billing.
**Impact:** The participant must repeatedly map project numbers back to internal change notifications, making parallel changes harder to trace.

> "Die sehe ich nie wieder, weder auf der Rechnung noch auf der Rückmeldung." - P04

## Possible Opportunity
Test persistent display of a customer-provided change ID alongside the TUV project ID in all statuses, messages, documents, and invoices.

# Pain Point: Customers Cannot Initiate UCI Requests Before Project Creation

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** Customers cannot create a request or significant-change record in UCI before TUV creates a project.
**Trigger:** A customer needs to start a new certification or significant-change request.
**Impact:** The first action depends on email or phone coordination and TUV setup rather than a customer-led, traceable workflow.
**Workaround:** Contact the project handler, exchange forms externally, and wait for a TUV-created project before uploading further material.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P10

**Representative Quotes:**
> "UCI nutzen wir. Ja, ist okay. Allerdings muss man ja immer zuerst in U.C.I. muss ja ein Projekt eröffnet werden, bevor man dann irgendwas übermitteln kann, selbst wenn ich jetzt 'ne neue Anfrage hatte, 'ne Significant Change oder so, die kann ich, ich persönlich oder als Kunde kann ich im U.C.I. nicht draufklicken, mach mir was Neues auf und füll das dann da drin an." - P10
>
> Translation: "We use UCI. It is okay. However, a project must first be opened in UCI before you can submit anything; even when I have a new request or a significant change, I personally, as the customer, cannot click in UCI, create a new item, and complete it there."

## Possible Opportunity
Provide customer-led request initiation with guided categorization, a submitted timestamp, and a linked handoff into the TUV project-creation workflow.

notes.title: Digitally Signed Forms Force Print-and-Scan
notes.body:
# Pain Point: Digitally Signed Forms Force Print-and-Scan

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** A digitally signed or write-protected TUV form cannot accept required customer information directly, so the customer must use a local PDF or paper workaround before re-signing and returning it.
**Trigger:** A customer needs to add a reference, such as an offer number, to a TUV-signed or write-protected form.
**Impact:** An otherwise digital commercial workflow becomes a manual local-document process and risks transcription, handling, or version errors.
**Workaround:** Print and scan the form, or create a local editable PDF, enter the information, sign it, and upload it again.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P10, P11

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Das kann ich aber nicht eintragen, weil das PDF digital signiert ist vom TÜV. Das kann ich nicht ändern. Das kann ich aber auch nicht als PDF drucken. Das muss ich ausdrucken und scannen." - P10
>
> Translation: "I cannot enter that because the PDF is digitally signed by TUV. I cannot change it, nor can I print it as a PDF. I have to print and scan it."

> "Eure Quotation ist unterschrieben und schreibgeschutzt. Ich muss mir die runterladen, dann druck ich mir die noch mal ins PDF, damit die nicht mehr schreibgeschutzt ist." - P11
>
> Translation: "Your quotation is signed and write-protected. I have to download it and print it again as a PDF so that it is no longer write-protected."

## Possible Opportunity
Replace post-signature PDF annotation with structured customer reference fields and a sequential digital-signature flow.

# Pain Point: Documents Are Not Grouped by Service

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** Documents from multiple service requests can become unmanageable when they are listed together and named inconsistently.
**Trigger:** A request contains multiple services and accumulates documents.
**Impact:** The participant cannot reliably tell which document belongs to which service.
**Workaround:** None stated.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Wenn ich dort alle Dokumente gelistet habe, weiß ich nicht mehr, welches zu welchem gehört. Das ist unmöglich." - P02
>
> Translation: "If I have all documents listed there, I no longer know which belongs to which. That is impossible."

## Possible Opportunity
Test service-level document grouping and consistent system-generated naming before relying on a combined document list.

notes.title: High-Effort Appendix ABC Maintenance
notes.body:
# Pain Point: High-Effort Appendix ABC Maintenance

**Theme:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]
**Description:** Keeping Appendix ABC current is labor-intensive for a large, dynamically changing device portfolio.
**Trigger:** New or changing devices and codes require updates to the Appendix ABC file.
**Impact:** Significant recurring manual effort to maintain certification data.
**Workaround:** Maintain the file in Excel and create successive revisions after freezes.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 20
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07, P08, P09, P10, P11

**Representative Quotes:**
> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated." - P01

> "It is very tough because we have some thousands of code and then the number of devices is very high." - P01

> "Das ist ein Riesenaufwand schon." - P02
>
> Translation: "That alone is a huge effort."

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel." - P02
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel."

> "The Appendix ABC is really difficult to be maintained." - P03

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch." - P04
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."

> "So now we're having to go back through now and do a complete assessment of the 10,000 CFNs and ensure that you know everything is accurate." - P05

> "The one that comes to mind most prominently is probably Appendix C for the suppliers." - P05

> "Wir haben halt auch immer so, sag ich mal, doppelt und dreifach Pflege, weil jemand muss es ja auch in die Health Canada Datenbank eintragen, dann müssen wir es noch mal in das Appendix A. B. C. eintragen und dann noch mal in unser System eintragen." - P06
>
> Translation: "We also always have double and triple maintenance, because someone has to enter it in the Health Canada database, then we have to enter it again in Appendix ABC, and then again in our system."

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam." - P06
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen." - P07
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind." - P07
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio." - P08
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."

> "Also zum einen ist es, es sind es die Funktionen in der Excel-Liste, die limitiert sind, wenn man an mehrere 1000 Artikelnummern kommt." - P09
>
> Translation: "The functions in the Excel list are limited when you reach several thousand article numbers."

> "Wenn sich ein Zertifikat ändert, muss der Datensatz viermal angepasst werden, wo wurde vielleicht in einer Liste nicht angepasst, wurde vergessen, dann haben wir 2 Wahrheiten, welches Zertifikat gilt jetzt, das hat auch schon zu vielen Fragen geführt." - P09
>
> Translation: "When a certificate changes, the record has to be adjusted four times; perhaps one list was not updated or was forgotten, and then we have two versions of the truth about which certificate applies, which has already led to many questions."

> "Das, das, das, das meiste ist, glaube ich, dass man alles wieder neu eintragen muss, ja, weil sich ja gefühlt alle drei Wochen die Version oder Revision." - P10
>
> Translation: "The main issue is that you have to enter everything again because it feels as though the version or revision changes every three weeks."

> "Man muss eigentlich jede Zeile, jede Spalte, jede Zelle angucken, was man da jetzt wirklich eintragen muss." - P10
>
> Translation: "You essentially have to look at every row, every column, and every cell to determine what must be entered."

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen." - P11
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

> "Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer." - P11
>
> Translation: "The main pain points at present are that we have to maintain three appendices, in whatever form."

## Possible Opportunity
Test bulk update and reuse mechanisms that preserve Appendix ABC's function as a technical-data summary.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Incomplete Change Impact Assessment Causes Resubmission

**Theme:** [[Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change]]
**Description:** Change coordinators can omit affected departments or assessments, and the gap is found only after submission or during implementation planning.
**Trigger:** A cross-functional change is assessed without all affected departments and activities being included from the start.
**Impact:** The change must be revised, implementation can be postponed, and the customer and notified body repeat work.
**Workaround:** Transfer change coordination to QMS and use monthly meetings to clarify borderline changes before formal submission.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 3
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative Quotes:**
> "The mistakes happen mostly due to communication. Because sometimes during a project, for example, during a change, some departments are not included." - P03

> "If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body." - P03

## Possible Opportunity
Test a change-impact workflow that makes affected functions, required assessments, and notified-body implications explicit before submission.

notes.title: Opaque Cost and Assessment Scope
notes.body:
# Pain Point: Opaque Cost and Assessment Scope

**Theme:** [[Unpredictable Commercial Scoping]]
**Description:** The customer cannot see a clear cost breakdown for reviews or reliably predict and contest assessment modules included in a quotation.
**Trigger:** Estimating a new certification, change, or annual routine cost before committing budget.
**Impact:** Cost estimates can change substantially, making budget planning unreliable and leaving the customer unable to influence assessment scope.
**Workaround:** Ask repeatedly for rationale and either accept the quoted scope or delay the work.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 4
**Interview IDs:** P02, P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Und da haben wir auch keinen Durchblick in den Kosten, was da zusammenkommt." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we have no visibility into the costs that add up there."

> "Ich kann es dann akzeptieren oder nicht? Da habe ich als Hersteller gar keine Macht." - P02
>
> Translation: "I can then accept it or not? As a manufacturer, I have no power at all."

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?" - P07
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

## Possible Opportunity
Test an itemized pre-quotation breakdown that links each assessment module to the change rationale and shows the cost effect.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Project Notification Subscriptions Cannot Be Scoped

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** Project visibility and notification subscriptions are coupled, so administrators receive alerts for projects they need permission to see but do not personally manage.
**Trigger:** An administrator manages access across a shared company profile containing projects owned by multiple locations and colleagues.
**Impact:** High volumes of irrelevant notifications consume attention and make relevant project messages harder to identify.
**Workaround:** Manually inspect and dismiss notifications while retaining broad access rights.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P09

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich überhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

> "Wenn ich da 'ne Möglichkeit hätte zu sagen, ich kann alle Projekte sehen, aber die Mitteilung zu den 5 Projekten, die möchte ich nicht haben, das zu deaktivieren, das wär super. Ich glaub, es geht technisch nicht." - P09
>
> Translation: "If I could say that I can see all projects but disable notifications for five of them, that would be excellent. I do not think that is technically possible."

## Possible Opportunity
Separate view and administration permissions from configurable notification subscriptions by project, owner, or customer-side responsibility.

notes.title: Request Follow-up Requires External Email
notes.body:
# Pain Point: Request Follow-up Requires External Email

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** When an application request is pending, the participant must switch to email because UCI does not let her continue the request conversation in context.
**Trigger:** A submitted request needs a reminder or follow-up.
**Impact:** Follow-up context is split between UCI and email, adding administrative effort and making request history harder to trace.
**Workaround:** Refer to the request number and date in a separate email.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Ich kann den Request nicht aufgreifen. Das heißt, ich muss auf das E-Mail zurückkommen, um den Request mit der Nummer zum Glück dann aufzugreifen und auch das Datum nochmals aufzugreifen, um das zu reminden." - P02
>
> Translation: "I cannot pick up the request again. That means I have to return to email to pick up the request with its number and date again in order to send a reminder."

## Possible Opportunity
Test request-linked messages and reminders that preserve the request number, current status, and conversation history.

# Pain Point: Restricted Appendix Rows Force Parallel Reference Lists

**Theme:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]
**Description:** Fixed spreadsheet row permissions prevent the participant from inserting or deleting required product references in place, so the detailed reference list must be maintained in a separate synchronized attachment.
**Trigger:** A high-volume certificate needs a new, removed, or changed product reference.
**Impact:** Parallel reference lists increase manual synchronization work and make the complete product set harder to review.
**Workaround:** Maintain a separate reference-number appendix at the same version as Appendix ABC.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P04

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Wir haben aber die Ref-Nummern dann noch mal in einem von uns selber erstellten Anhang, den wir dann immer parallel noch pflegen und mitschicken." - P04
>
> Translation: "We keep the reference numbers again in a separately created appendix, which we maintain in parallel and send along."

> "Die eingeschränkten Rechte, also dass ich nicht Zeilen hinzufügen kann oder löschen kann." - P04
>
> Translation: "The restricted permissions, meaning that I cannot add or delete rows."

## Possible Opportunity
Test structured records that allow authorized additions, removals, and relationship updates without creating a parallel reference list.

notes.title: Reviewer Feedback Requires Revision Realignment
notes.body:
# Pain Point: Reviewer Feedback Requires Revision Realignment

**Theme:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]]
**Description:** Reviewer comments, template changes, and customer working copies can create concurrent Appendix ABC states that require manual realignment into the active version.
**Trigger:** TUV SUD reviews or updates an Appendix while the customer continues work, or a revised template arrives alongside a customer revision.
**Impact:** Rework and risk of inconsistent data across customer and reviewer versions.
**Workaround:** Re-update the active revision after comments arrive and maintain an internal sequence of submitted and working versions.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 15
**Interview IDs:** P01, P04, P05, P06, P07, P08, P09, P10, P11

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file." - P01

> "Die Versionierung ist sehr, sehr schwierig." - P04
>
> Translation: "Versioning is very, very difficult."

> "Dann habe ich parallel eben die Arbeitsversion V24." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I have the working version V24 running in parallel."

> "Then they would kind of maintain like the most up-to-date versions on their end. So that part's a bit confusing to me, I suppose." - P05

> "We also have tech doc reviews going on where we're being asked to change the appendices from that. So we've got multiple sources asking for changes at the same time." - P05

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist." - P07
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

> "Und da haben wir auch häufig den Fall, wir haben intern und Sie haben Änderungen gemacht und sich dann hinzusetzen und das wieder alles in eine Datei zu bringen, das ist wirklich viel Arbeit und auch fehleranfällig, dass der Kunde dann schreibt: 'O.K., meine Änderungen sind jetzt irgendwie nicht mehr in der Tabelle drinne.'" - P09
>
> Translation: "We often have the case where we made changes internally and you also made changes, and sitting down to bring everything back into one file is a lot of work and error-prone, so a colleague then writes that their changes are somehow no longer in the table."

> "Gefühlt immer. Also ich warte immer, bis ich den letzten kriege." - P10
>
> Translation: "It feels like it happens all the time. I always wait until I receive the latest version."

> "Wenn wir Änderungen machen, dann sagen wir: 'Führ das bitte zusammen und schick mir die dann.' Das dauert aber dann auch." - P10
>
> Translation: "When we make changes, we say: please consolidate it and then send it to me. But that also takes time."

> "Wir haben immer eine offene Draftversion, da wird fleissig eingetragen, was so kommt, bis der Tag kommt, wo so, jetzt mussen wir mal ein Update schicken." - P11
>
> Translation: "We always have an open draft version where changes are entered until the day comes when we must send an update."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

## Possible Opportunity
Test shared revision states, review comments linked to a record, and explicit reconciliation flows.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Service Request Submission Timestamp Is Missing

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** A submitted service request shows its last-edited state rather than a clear submission timestamp.
**Trigger:** The customer checks when a service request was transmitted while waiting for TUV follow-up or project creation.
**Impact:** The customer cannot verify the start of the waiting period or answer internal questions about why no response has arrived.
**Workaround:** Reconstruct the submission date from memory or other records.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P09

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Das hab ich auch schon mal angemerkt, dass man da nicht sehen kann, wann der Service Request wirklich übermittelt wurde. Ich glaub, da steht nur 'zuletzt bearbeitet' Stand oder sowas wird angezeigt." - P09
>
> Translation: "I have already pointed out that you cannot see when the service request was actually submitted. I think it only shows a 'last edited' status or something similar."

## Possible Opportunity
Show an immutable submitted-at timestamp and acknowledgement alongside the editable request history.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Submitted Request Documents Disappear from Projects

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** Application documents submitted through the service portal are not visible after UCI creates the related project.
**Trigger:** A submitted service request is converted into an active project.
**Impact:** Users must search their own records to verify what they originally submitted, weakening project traceability.
**Workaround:** Retrieve the original documents from internal storage.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P08, P09

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Wenn das Projekt angelegt wurde, ich sehe die Antragsunterlagen nicht mehr in U.C.I." - P08
>
> Translation: "When the project has been created, I can no longer see the application documents in UCI."

> "Wenn ich im kompletten Projekt alles drin hab, dass auch jemand, den ich aufs Projekt zugreifen lasse, auch dann die ganzen Application Form sehen kann, was wir beantragt haben." - P09
>
> Translation: "When everything is in the complete project, someone whom I give project access should also be able to see all the application forms showing what we requested."

## Possible Opportunity
Preserve submitted request documents as read-only, project-linked records once a request becomes a project.

# Pain Point: UCI Notifications Require Download to Mark as Read

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** A UCI document notification cannot be acknowledged as read without downloading the document.
**Trigger:** A user sees a document notification that does not require a local download.
**Impact:** Users create unnecessary files and extra actions merely to clear a notification state.
**Workaround:** Download the document even when it is not needed locally.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P10

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Dann sehe ich halt eine Notification. Die kann ich aber heute nicht gefühlt nicht als gelesen aktivieren. Die muss ich mir runterladen. Die will ich aber gar nicht runterladen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Then I see a notification. At present, I do not feel that I can mark it as read. I have to download it, although I do not want to download it."

## Possible Opportunity
Allow users to view and explicitly acknowledge a notification without creating a local document copy.

notes.title: Unclear Certification Step Timing
notes.body:
# Pain Point: Unclear Certification Step Timing

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** The participant understands the major certification phases but cannot reliably see timing or the current status from one step to the next.
**Trigger:** Managing an active certification request across departments and project types.
**Impact:** Uncertainty about progress, expected certificate timing, and whether TUV has received or reviewed a submission.
**Workaround:** Personally track project steps in Excel and ask the auditor.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 11
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P04, P05, P06, P07, P09, P10

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear." - P01

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie?" - P02
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, and when do they begin?"

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten." - P06
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

> "Wir haben zum Beispiel dieses Jahr im Audit erlebt, dass die Auditoren in einer Version vom Appendix A. B. C. nachgeschaut haben, die total outdated war." - P07
>
> Translation: "This year during the audit, the auditors reviewed a version of Appendix ABC that was completely outdated."

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?" - P07
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"

> "Was für uns aber das zentrale Datum ist es nicht, wann wir 'ne Rechnung erhalten, sondern wann wir das Approval kriegen." - P09
>
> Translation: "For us, the central date is not when we receive an invoice, but when we receive approval."

> "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. fürs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prüfung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prüfung, das ist O.K. Ich wüsste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen könnte in der Übersicht. Das wäre ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TÜV. Das sieht man primär nicht." - P10
>
> Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; Dornier owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."

> "Aber sagen wir mal, die Zwischendinger die Zwischenmeilensteine, die sieht man jetzt aktuell nicht in der Übersicht, wo du sagst, okay, der TÜV antwortet bis dahin oder wir müssen dann bis 90 Tage danach oder was auch immer dann ein Feedback geben, dass man sowas auch in der Übersicht sieht." - P10
>
> Translation: "The intermediate milestones are not currently visible in the overview, such as when TUV will respond or when we must give feedback within 90 days."

## Possible Opportunity
Validate which status changes and forecast dates would be useful and reliable enough to display.

sections.Evidence:
**Evidence Count:** 11
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P04, P05, P06, P07, P09, P10

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear." - P01

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie?" - P02
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, and when do they begin?"

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten." - P06
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

> "Wir haben zum Beispiel dieses Jahr im Audit erlebt, dass die Auditoren in einer Version vom Appendix A. B. C. nachgeschaut haben, die total outdated war." - P07
>
> Translation: "This year during the audit, the auditors reviewed a version of Appendix ABC that was completely outdated."

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?" - P07
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"

> "Was für uns aber das zentrale Datum ist es nicht, wann wir 'ne Rechnung erhalten, sondern wann wir das Approval kriegen." - P09
>
> Translation: "For us, the central date is not when we receive an invoice, but when we receive approval."

> "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. fürs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prüfung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prüfung, das ist O.K. Ich wüsste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen könnte in der Übersicht. Das wäre ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TÜV. Das sieht man primär nicht." - P10
>
> Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; Dornier owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."

> "Aber sagen wir mal, die Zwischendinger die Zwischenmeilensteine, die sieht man jetzt aktuell nicht in der Übersicht, wo du sagst, okay, der TÜV antwortet bis dahin oder wir müssen dann bis 90 Tage danach oder was auch immer dann ein Feedback geben, dass man sowas auch in der Übersicht sieht." - P10
>
> Translation: "The intermediate milestones are not currently visible in the overview, such as when TUV will respond or when we must give feedback within 90 days."

# Pain Point: Unclear Invoice Timing Delays Administrative Closure

**Theme:** [[Unclear Commercial Closure and Support]]
**Description:** The completion point of a service and timing of associated invoices are unclear or delayed.

notes.title: Automated Certification Data Checks
notes.body:
# Need: Automated Certification Data Checks

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Validate certification data automatically and remind accountable users when supplier certificates or required attributes need attention; offer consequential changes as explicit user-confirmed proposals rather than silently applying them.
**Related Theme:** [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

## Evidence
> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion." - P04
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."

> "Wenn ich das und das eintrage, hat es diese Prüfung zur Ursache, also dass ich dann mache, wenn ich so eingebe, was halt richtig ist oder was falsch ist, also dass ich es selber erkennen kann." - P06
>
> Translation: "If I enter this or that, it causes this assessment, so I should be able to recognize myself whether what I enter is right or wrong."

> "Gibt es dann so eine Art Vorprüfung oder sonst irgendwas? Geht es in die Richtung, wo ich mir wünschen würde, als Kunde vielleicht dazu sagen, ich schicke das einfach mal zum Check ein und es läuft durch und gibt mir dann die formalen Punkte." - P10
>
> Translation: "Could there be some kind of preliminary check? I would like to submit something for a check and have it identify the formal issues."

> "Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut." - P11
>
> Translation: "The AI could say that a related item also needs changing and ask whether it should do that; I could actively choose yes or no, and that would be acceptable or even good."

notes.title: Guided Service-Specific Submission Requirements
notes.body:
# Need: Guided Service-Specific Submission Requirements

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Select the intended service or change scenario and receive the exact required fields, documents, definitions, and examples for that scenario rather than interpreting generic forms or repeatedly asking a contact.
**Related Theme:** [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

## Evidence
> "Wenn ich jetzt eine Neuproduktanmeldung habe, was brauchen Sie dafür noch mit dazu, reicht da nur die IFQ, wollen Sie da gleich Broschüren haben oder sonstige Informationen?" - P06
>
> Translation: "If I have a new product registration, what else do you need for it? Is the IFQ enough, or do you also want brochures or other information?"

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"

> "Wenn es da noch irgendwie was an die Hand geben könnte, wie so ein Fallbaum. Ich ändere das, ich ändere das." - P09
>
> Translation: "It would help to have something like a decision tree: I change this, I change that."

> "Wenn ich sage, nein, wünscht ihr was, dann habe ich 'ne Plattform, heißt die U.C.I. oder wie auch immer und ich logge mich ein und sage, ich mache 'ne new Application und dann wähle ich aus, will ich jetzt mein Ist es produktbezogen, ist es QM-System bezogen und ich habe eine gewisse Logik dahinter und ich werde dementsprechend durchgeführt." - P10
>
> Translation: "If I could wish for it, I would have a platform where I log in, create a new application, choose whether it concerns a product or the quality-management system, and am guided by the appropriate logic."

> "Wenn ich jetzt bei einem den Eintrag eher fuge einen E. R. C. Code fur diese Seite hinzu und wenn da jetzt ein Icon ware, Information, Achtung, ERC Codes, blablabla, einfach so ein bisschen und ein paar Links, ja klar, ware naturlich immer toll." - P11
>
> Translation: "If I add an ERC code for a site, it would be helpful to have an information icon with guidance and links about ERC codes."

notes.title: Role-Based Certification Data Governance
notes.body:
# Need: Role-Based Certification Data Governance

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Assign scoped manufacturer contributor, approver, and notified-body reviewer roles so each party can view or act on certification data without losing ownership or accountability.
**Related Theme:** [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

## Evidence
> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht." - P07
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."

> "Was da drin steht, gehört zu uns." - P07
>
> Translation: "What is in it belongs to us."

> "Dann vielleicht auch mit dem Status 'ne klare Abgrenzung, was dürfen wir umsetzen, also welchen Status dürfen wir ändern und welchen Status dürfen wir nicht setzen, also dass wir gar nicht die Möglichkeit haben, vielleicht was auf Covered by Certificate oder Ähnlichem zu setzen, weil das 'ne reine TÜV-Offline wäre." - P09
>
> Translation: "Statuses should clearly distinguish what we may change and what we may not set, so that we cannot set something to 'Covered by Certificate' because that would be solely for TUV."

> "Meiner Meinung nach hat der Hersteller die Datenhoheit, weil es unsere Daten sind." - P10
>
> Translation: "In my opinion, the manufacturer has data sovereignty because they are our data."

> "Wir haben fur die R. A. Mitarbeiter im Prinzip Adminrechte, also die sehen einfach alle Projekte und konnen uberall auch andern und eintragen und Messages schreiben." - P11
>
> Translation: "Our Regulatory Affairs employees essentially have administrator rights: they see all projects and can change, enter, and write messages everywhere."

notes.title: Traceable Shared Data Review History
notes.body:
# Need: Traceable Shared Data Review History

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** See, at field level, who entered, changed, reviewed, or commented on shared certification data, while preserving an approved manufacturer-controlled record.
**Related Theme:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]]

## Evidence
> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "In der Datenbank könnte ich mir ja gut vorstellen, dass man das über Status abfangen kann. Also Entered by Manufacturer, Reviewed by Notified Body, Feedback by Notified Body oder so." - P07
>
> Translation: "In a database, I could imagine handling this through statuses: entered by manufacturer, reviewed by notified body, feedback by notified body, or similar."

> "Also nachvollziehbar über 'ne Änderungshistorie wäre wichtig, dass man letzten Endes sieht, was ist an dem Datensatz aktuell geändert worden oder was ist in der Änderung und mit welchem Bezug zu einem zu welchem Projekt ist das gerade in der Änderung?" - P09
>
> Translation: "A traceable change history would be important so that one can see what has been changed in the record, what is currently being changed, and which project the change relates to."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

# Need: User-Confirmed Certification Data Automation

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Receive suggested consequential updates and select whether to apply them, rather than allowing automation to change certification records independently.
**Related Theme:** [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

## Evidence
> "Also automatisierte Anpassungen wurde ich gerne ausschliessen. Wenn dann mit Frage." - P11
>
> Translation: "I would like to exclude automated changes. If anything, they should happen with a question."

> "Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut." - P11
>
> Translation: "The AI could say that a related item also needs changing and ask whether it should do that; I could actively choose yes or no, and that would be acceptable or even good."

notes.title: Visible Certification Timing
notes.body:
# Need: Visible Certification Timing

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** See the timing and current step of the certification process.
**Related Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]

## Evidence
> "I think it will be very important to know the time, to know the step of the certification process." - P01

> "Was man nicht hat, ist den Request Progress." - P02
>
> Translation: "What one does not have is the request progress."

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months."

> "Changes, assessment status, also deficiency status... timelines regarding the status, the expected closure date." - P03

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "Was für uns aber das zentrale Datum ist es nicht, wann wir 'ne Rechnung erhalten, sondern wann wir das Approval kriegen." - P09
>
> Translation: "For us, the central date is not when we receive an invoice, but when we receive approval."

> "Aber sagen wir mal, die Zwischendinger die Zwischenmeilensteine, die sieht man jetzt aktuell nicht in der Übersicht, wo du sagst, okay, der TÜV antwortet bis dahin oder wir müssen dann bis 90 Tage danach oder was auch immer dann ein Feedback geben, dass man sowas auch in der Übersicht sieht." - P10
>
> Translation: "The intermediate milestones are not currently visible in the overview, such as when TUV will respond or when we must give feedback within 90 days."

notes.title: Insight Status
notes.body:
# Insight Status

Updated: 2026-07-30

- Theme [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]: P10 provides a tenth direct confirmation; frequent revisions and MDR/MDD structure differences force repeated cell-by-cell entry. Linked to [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]].
- Theme [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]]: P10 provides an eighth direct confirmation; participants still wait for TUV to consolidate the latest file. Linked to [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]].
- Theme [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]: P10 provides a tenth direct confirmation. UCI is useful after project setup, but customer-led request initiation, task ownership, intermediate milestones, notification acknowledgement, and locked form completion remain incomplete. Linked to [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]].
- Theme [[Unclear Commercial Closure and Support]]: P02 supplies related pre-quotation evidence only; not yet enough connected, cross-interview evidence for an insight.
- Theme [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]: P10 provides a tenth direct confirmation and adds standardized integration, directly editable records, and automated formal pre-checks; linked to [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]] and [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]].
- Theme [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]: P10 provides a ninth direct confirmation that long-term named contacts remain valuable alongside digital workflows; linked to [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]].
- Theme [[Unpredictable Commercial Scoping]]: P09 adds related evidence about documents requested during assessment, but does not directly confirm missing pre-quotation cost or module rationale. Counts remain unchanged and no insight is justified.
- Theme [[Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change]]: one interview supports this preliminary theme; no insight is justified yet.

- Theme [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]: P11 provides an eleventh direct confirmation; teams copy one updated Appendix into multiple related projects and the general repository. Linked to [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]].
- Theme [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]]: P11 provides a ninth direct confirmation; an open draft still relies on manual highlighting and change history. Linked to [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]].
- Theme [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]: P11 adds related positive evidence that shared UCI project access works; it does not establish a new visibility pain or change counts. Linked to [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]].
- Theme [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]: P11 provides an eleventh direct confirmation that source synchronization must respect approval gates and automation must wait for explicit confirmation. Linked to [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]] and [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]].
- Theme [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]: P11 provides a tenth direct confirmation that recurring human coordination works well. Linked to [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]].
- Themes [[Unclear Commercial Closure and Support]], [[Unpredictable Commercial Scoping]], and [[Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change]]: P11 provides related or no direct evidence only; no new insight is justified.

[[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]] is supported by direct evidence across eleven interviews and two high-confidence themes. [[Use Reusable Structured Certification Data]] is its single anchored recommendation. [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]] is supported by nine direct cross-company confirmations of revision reconciliation plus high-confidence structured-collaboration and manual-maintenance themes; [[Make Review Feedback a Traceable Permissioned Workflow]] is its single anchored recommendation. [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]] is supported by high-confidence visibility and guidance themes across ten interviews; [[Pair Action Alerts with Human Escalation]] is its single anchored recommendation. P11 does not justify a new insight or recommendation.
