notes.title: Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source

frontmatter.name: Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source

notes.body:
# Insight: Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source

**Insight:** The burden of Appendix ABC is not its certification purpose but maintaining overlapping product data manually across internal systems, multiple Appendix structures, and EUDAMED. Customers need a reusable structured source that carries shared product data forward while preserving certificate-specific relationships and fields.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information." - P03

> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information." - P01

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export." - P04
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."

> "We have that metadata within, you know, our own systems." - P05

> "I think if there's a better system for keeping things maintained and avoiding unintentional changes that then cause some synchronization issues, that would be preferable too." - P05

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden." - P06
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise." - P08
>
> Translation: "We cannot simply press a button and tell it to take the data from a particular database on our side and put it into the table in a particular way."

> "Das ist natürlich auch unser Wunsch, dass man 'ne Situation hat, wo man bei uns in der in der Datenbank 'ne Information einträgt und der Datensatz, wenn er dann komplett ist, halt auch transferiert werden kann, so wie das für die Eutermed auch funktioniert, dass man da nichts händisch eintragen muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "Our wish is to enter information in our database and transfer the record once it is complete, as with EUDAMED, so that nothing has to be entered manually."

> "Wenn man das nicht auf Artikelnummer Ebene eintragen muss, sondern für einen Basic U.D.I., das würde uns natürlich schon sehr helfen." - P09
>
> Translation: "If data did not have to be entered at article-number level but could instead be managed for a Basic UDI, that would help us greatly."

> "Wenn jetzt die Schnittstelle ein Standardformat ist, das wäre natürlich sehr gut." - P10
>
> Translation: "If the interface used a standard format, that would naturally be very good."

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen." - P11
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

**Business Impact:** Manual, duplicated data maintenance consumes regulatory and quality capacity and increases the chance of inconsistent certification records. P04 through P11 show that customers with structured leading systems still incur this cost when TUV inputs must be manually assembled into separate lists or synchronized across changing sources and projects.
**Design Implication:** Treat certification data as reusable structured records with imports or integrations, rather than as independently maintained spreadsheet copies. Prefill fields from EUDAMED where they overlap, support Basic UDI-level reuse rather than unnecessary article-level duplication, then guide users through remaining certificate-specific data. Support both standardized system-to-system integration for mature data environments and bulk import for others, with validation that identifies incomplete or incompatible data before submission. Synchronize source changes only once their regulatory approval state permits their use in certification records.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

fields.Design Implication: Treat certification data as reusable structured records with imports or integrations, rather than as independently maintained spreadsheet copies. Prefill fields from EUDAMED where they overlap, support Basic UDI-level reuse rather than unnecessary article-level duplication, then guide users through remaining certificate-specific data. Support both standardized system-to-system integration for mature data environments and bulk import for others, with validation that identifies incomplete or incompatible data before submission. Synchronize source changes only once their regulatory approval state permits their use in certification records.

Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export.
We have that metadata within, you know, our own systems.

Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise.

Das ist natürlich auch unser Wunsch, dass man 'ne Situation hat, wo man bei uns in der in der Datenbank 'ne Information einträgt und der Datensatz, wenn er dann komplett ist, halt auch transferiert werden kann, so wie das für die Eutermed auch funktioniert, dass man da nichts händisch eintragen muss.

notes.title: Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation
notes.body:
# Insight: Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation

**Insight:** Self-service certification visibility is valuable only when action-required events are reliably surfaced and paired with a reachable human escalation path. Status tools reduce routine follow-up, but missed system-only deficiency alerts and opaque final certification-body review can delay work unless personal communication remains available.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]], [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "Ich kenn es schon aus der Vergangenheit bei anderen Unternehmen, wenn ich von den Systemen so viele Bling und Bings und hier ist was geschehen und hier ist was geschehen, dann habe ich also schon mehrfach überlegt, da gibt es so 'n Overflow und was passiert, keiner erfasst die Sachen mehr, weil es zu viel Bling, Bling und Bing und Bang ist." - P06
>
> Translation: "I know from the past at other companies that when systems produce so many pings and notifications that something happened, there is an overflow and nobody notices things anymore because there is too much pinging."

> "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich überhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

> "Ich finde, wir sind eigentlich schon ziemlich gut in der Kommunikation, jetzt insbesondere durch U.C.I. die Frau Einemann als zentrale Ansprechpartnerin, also da dauert es keinen halben Tag, hat man 'ne Antwort oder zumindest, ich hab's weitergegeben, ich kümmere mich drum." - P09
>
> Translation: "I think communication is already quite good, especially through UCI and Ms. Einemann as the central contact; it takes less than half a day to receive an answer or at least confirmation that it has been forwarded and will be handled."

> "Ich möchte meinen Project Handler oder meinen Relationship Manager, wie auch immer, rein. Nicht dass ich zuerst durch muss und sitz dann wie gefühlt die 10 Minuten in der Warteschlange." - P10
>
> Translation: "I want to bring in my project handler or relationship manager, rather than first having to go through a process and wait in a queue for ten minutes."

**Business Impact:** Delayed awareness of questions can extend review timelines, while unnecessary status-chasing consumes both customer and TUV capacity. P06, P09, and P10 show that visibility also fails when notification acknowledgement is cumbersome or when users cannot quickly reach a named contact for complex questions.
**Design Implication:** Provide a status workspace with high-salience, acknowledged alerts for required action, and retain direct project-linked contact and escalation routes for questions that need judgement. Decouple notification subscriptions from view or administration rights, allow read acknowledgement without forced downloads, and suppress routine change noise through project-, owner-, and responsibility-based preferences and summaries.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

frontmatter.name: Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle

notes.body:
# Insight: Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle

**Insight:** Reusable certification data alone will not remove rework if manufacturer working copies, notified-body feedback, and template revisions evolve independently. Shared records need a controlled lifecycle that makes each party's role, review status, feedback, and field-level changes visible without allowing one party to silently overwrite another's accountable record.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]], [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon." - P04
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

> "Dann vielleicht auch mit dem Status 'ne klare Abgrenzung, was dürfen wir umsetzen, also welchen Status dürfen wir ändern und welchen Status dürfen wir nicht setzen, also dass wir gar nicht die Möglichkeit haben, vielleicht was auf Covered by Certificate oder Ähnlichem zu setzen, weil das 'ne reine TÜV-Offline wäre." - P09
>
> Translation: "Statuses should clearly distinguish what we may change and what we may not set, so that we cannot set something to 'Covered by Certificate' because that would be solely for TUV."

> "Also nachvollziehbar über 'ne Änderungshistorie wäre wichtig, dass man letzten Endes sieht, was ist an dem Datensatz aktuell geändert worden oder was ist in der Änderung und mit welchem Bezug zu einem zu welchem Projekt ist das gerade in der Änderung?" - P09
>
> Translation: "A traceable change history would be important so that one can see what has been changed in the record, what is currently being changed, and which project the change relates to."

> "Dann unter Umständen, wenn es unsere Daten sind, dann vielleicht irgendeine Acknowledgement-Genehmigung oder sonst irgendwas." - P10
>
> Translation: "When it is our data, there should perhaps be some acknowledgement or approval."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

> "Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut." - P11
>
> Translation: "The AI could say that a related item also needs changing and ask whether it should do that; I could actively choose yes or no, and that would be acceptable or even good."

**Business Impact:** Manual reconciliation consumes regulatory and quality capacity, can lose reviewer feedback between versions, and creates inconsistent certification records even when the source product data itself is correct. P11 shows that teams also spend effort preserving change provenance through manual formatting and need consequential automation to remain accountable.
**Design Implication:** Model review as a permissioned state workflow on shared records: manufacturer entries and releases, notified-body review and feedback, party-specific status authority, non-destructive validation, field-level provenance, project-linked change history, and a visible path to resolve and approve changes. Require manufacturer acknowledgement before notified-body changes affect manufacturer-owned content, and require explicit confirmation before automation applies consequential related changes. Link assessed exemplars to all records covered by the same change so approval closes the declared scope without manual follow-up.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Positive Pattern: Responsive Auditor Guidance

**Theme:** [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]
**Process Phase:** Request/Application; Change; Review
**Description:** Named notified-body contacts provide document lists and recurring meetings that clarify requirements before and during certification activity.
**Why it works:** Participants know whom to contact, receive actionable information requests, and can resolve borderline questions before formal submission.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A digital workflow could remove valuable tailored guidance if it offers only static forms or generic help.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 12
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07, P09, P10

**Representative Quotes:**
> "With Daria, we are quite well informed about the information needed." - P01

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity." - P01

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen." - P02
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "Wir haben 'nen ungefähr 'nen monatlichen Call, wo aber dann auch Quality Sterility Assurance dabei ist, wo unsere offenen Themen besprochen werden." - P04
>
> Translation: "We have an approximately monthly call that also includes Quality and Sterility Assurance, where our open topics are discussed."

> "We have a weekly meeting with our project handler and coordinator." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung." - P06
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut." - P07
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."

> "Ich finde, wir sind eigentlich schon ziemlich gut in der Kommunikation, jetzt insbesondere durch U.C.I. die Frau Einemann als zentrale Ansprechpartnerin, also da dauert es keinen halben Tag, hat man 'ne Antwort oder zumindest, ich hab's weitergegeben, ich kümmere mich drum." - P09
>
> Translation: "I think communication is already quite good, especially through UCI and Ms. Einemann as the central contact; it takes less than half a day to receive an answer or at least confirmation that it has been forwarded and will be handled."

> "Das funktioniert aber eigentlich auch gut, da haben wir auch die Vereinbarung, wir sagten, wann die Listen quasi eingefroren sind, dann gehen die an den Herr Kunte, der zieht die, migriert die mit einem Migration Tool oder irgendwas und dann kriegen wir sie wieder zur Verfügung gestellt und haben dann das neue Template verwendet mit den Daten aus der vorherigen Version." - P09
>
> Translation: "This actually works well: we agree when the lists are frozen, they go to Mr. Kunte, he migrates them with a migration tool, and we receive the new template containing the data from the previous version."

> "Das sind ja so Situationen, wo wir mit Herrn Klopp dann sprechen. Wir arbeiten im Herrn Klopp ja schon, wie gesagt, seit keine Ahnung, also sind es 8 Jahre, 10 Jahre irgendwie so was zusammen. Und ich glaube auch, dass das wir gut mit ihm reden können und irgendwie eine Frage ist, dann hilft er uns jedes Mal und dann ist es halt auch für uns jetzt halt einfach, er ist ein vertrauter Kontakt, dem kann man was fragen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Those are situations where we speak with Mr. Klopf. We have worked with him for eight or ten years, can talk to him well, and whenever there is a question, he helps us; he is simply a trusted contact whom we can ask."

## Update Note
Confidence increased from Medium to High after P09 added an eighth consistent interview with direct evidence of responsive named-contact support.

notes.title: TUV-Managed Appendix Template Migration
notes.body:
# Positive Pattern: TUV-Managed Appendix Template Migration

**Theme:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]]
**Process Phase:** Change
**Description:** The customer and TUV agree a freeze window, after which a named TUV contact migrates existing Appendix data into the new template and returns it.
**Why it works:** A clear handoff and tool-supported migration prevent the customer from manually rebuilding the new template.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** Customers could regain costly template-migration work; however, preserving this benefit should not preserve the temporary editing lock or parallel-version risk.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P09, P11

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Das funktioniert aber eigentlich auch gut, da haben wir auch die Vereinbarung, wir sagten, wann die Listen quasi eingefroren sind, dann gehen die an den Herr Kunte, der zieht die, migriert die mit einem Migration Tool oder irgendwas und dann kriegen wir sie wieder zur Verfügung gestellt und haben dann das neue Template verwendet mit den Daten aus der vorherigen Version." - P09
>
> Translation: "This actually works well: we agree when the lists are frozen, they go to Mr. Kunte, he migrates them with a migration tool, and we receive the new template containing the data from the previous version."

> "Da haben wir dann aber von euch ein Update bekommen, wo alle Daten schon migriert waren. Also das war naturlich unheimlich toll." - P11
>
> Translation: "We received an update from you in which all data had already been migrated. That was naturally extremely good."

## Update Note
Confidence: Low -> Medium, P11 added an independent direct confirmation that TUV-provided migration removes substantial customer work.

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b.

notes.title: UCI Centralizes Active Project Work
notes.body:
# Positive Pattern: UCI Centralizes Active Project Work

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Process Phase:** Request/Application; Review
**Description:** UCI centralizes electronic requests, project communication, and active-project documents for this participant group.
**Why it works:** Stakeholders can use a common project location instead of relying only on email recipients and individual inboxes.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A redesigned workflow could lose the existing project-level communication and document context while addressing gaps in request-to-project continuity.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 3
**Interview IDs:** P08, P09, P11

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Mit U.C.I. hat sich schon einiges verbessert, weil man da tatsächlich ja elektronisch diese Anträge stellen kann, dann auch zu diesen Projekten dann immer alles an einer Stelle in der Kommunikation und auch von den Projektdokumenten her hat." - P08
>
> Translation: "UCI has already improved quite a lot because applications can be submitted electronically and the communication and project documents are then all in one place for those projects."

> "Ansonsten, ja sonst, wenn die Projektplanung dann steht und die ganzen Module, wie Frau Conrad eben auch gesagt hat und das alles geplant ist, dann funktioniert das da ab für folgendes Tracking und Planen sehr gut und da haben wir tatsächlich nicht noch zusätzlich im Hintergrund bei uns auf unserer Seite Tools." - P09
>
> Translation: "Once the project plan and all the modules are set up, tracking and planning work very well from that point onward, and we do not use additional tools in the background on our side."

> "U. C. I. ist in dem Fall sehr gut, weil einfach alle Zugriff haben." - P11
>
> Translation: "UCI is very good in this case because everyone has access."

## Update Note
Confidence increased from Medium to High after P11 independently confirmed the value of shared active-project access.

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b.

# Proto-Segments

| Interview ID | Suspected Segment | Key Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Regulatory and quality assurance lead at a medical-device manufacturer | Primary contact with the certification body; manages a large, changing device portfolio; relies on Excel, ERP, technical documentation, and auditor guidance. |
| P02 | Regulatory Affairs Manager at a medical-device manufacturer | Primary certification contact and sole UCI user; consolidates technical documentation from subject-matter experts; maintains live Appendix ABC data and project/cost tracking in Excel. |
| P03 | Quality Management System Manager at a medical-device manufacturer | ISO 13485 management representative; owns QMS changes, audits, and quality-system communication; jointly maintains Appendix ABC with Regulatory Affairs. |
| P04 | Regulatory Affairs specialists at a large medical-device manufacturer | Coordinate notified-body applications and Appendix ABC across a large product portfolio; rely on SAP, Teamcenter, SharePoint, and cross-functional coordination. |
| P05 | Regulatory Affairs managers at a large medical-device manufacturer | Manage MDR remediation, Class III maintenance, renewals, and high-volume Appendix ABC data; rely on project-handler relationships, email, and partially adopted UCI workflows. |
| P06 | Regulatory Affairs leaders at a medical-device manufacturer | Manage MDR and MDSAP Appendix ABC records across global registrations; coordinate controlled document versions, PLM and external data, UCI submissions, and management-level project reporting. |
| P07 | Quality Management System lead at a medical-device manufacturer | Manages QMS applications, audits, certificates, and QMS changes; coordinates with Regulatory Affairs on controlled Appendix records, multiple data systems, and notified-body review. |
| P08 | Cross-functional certification stakeholders at a large medical-device manufacturer | Includes Quality Management, Audit Management, Regulatory Affairs authority management, and Regulatory Affairs labeling/data management; collectively maintain high-volume Appendix ABC data and coordinate UCI projects. |
| P09 | Cross-functional Regulatory Affairs and Global Quality Management team at a large medical-device manufacturer | Regulatory Affairs owns product files and Appendix data for about 120 devices; Global Quality Management coordinates TUV communication, distributed project access, and high-volume UCI tracking. |
| P10 | Senior Quality Management leaders at a global medical-device manufacturer | Direct Quality Management leaders coordinate notified-body communication, significant changes, audits, commercial approvals, distributed data, and strategic quality-system digitalization. |
| P11 | Regulatory Affairs team at a medical-device manufacturer | Maintains Appendix ABC across multiple product groups, coordinates approval-gated supplier and product changes, and manages shared UCI project work with controlled team access. |

A proto-persona has been created in `07_personas`: [[Regulatory Certification Lead]], supported by P01, P02, P04, P05, P06, and P11. P11 is a direct Regulatory Affairs-team confirmation of product-file ownership, Appendix maintenance, and certification-data governance. Persona splitting check after P10: P03, P07, and P10 are three role-specific QMS interviews with a consistent goal of governing audits, certificates, QMS changes, and notified-body coordination. Their responsibilities differ fundamentally from Regulatory Certification Leads' product-file and data-ownership focus, so [[Quality Management Certification Lead]] is created as a separate proto-persona. P08 and P09 remain mixed-role evidence of cross-functional collaboration rather than homogeneous support for either persona.

# Persona: Quality Management Certification Lead

**Segment:** Quality Management certification lead at a medical-device manufacturer
**Based on Interviews:** [[P03]], [[P07]], [[P10]]

## Context
Owns or coordinates quality-management system changes, audits, certificates, and notified-body communication. Connects Regulatory Affairs, Quality Management, operations, and external certification stakeholders while maintaining a controlled evidence trail across UCI, internal systems, shared files, and direct human contact.

P10 confirms that senior Quality Management leaders also oversee significant changes, commercial approvals, global quality-system operations, and quality-system digitalization. This role needs a strategic portfolio view but remains accountable for operationally actionable tasks, deadlines, and certification correspondence.

## Goals
- Keep audits, certificates, significant changes, and related actions traceable without reconstructing context across systems.
- Give accountable teams a clear view of current ownership, deadlines, and outstanding certification work.
- Preserve trusted access to notified-body experts while reducing document, email, and spreadsheet administration.

## Associated Themes

- [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]
- [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

- [[Customers Cannot Initiate UCI Requests Before Project Creation]]
- [[UCI Notifications Require Download to Mark as Read]]
- [[Digitally Signed Forms Force Print-and-Scan]]

- [[Visible Certification Timing]]
- [[In-Context Notification Acknowledgement]]
- [[Guided Service-Specific Submission Requirements]]

# Persona: Regulatory Certification Lead

**Segment:** Regulatory certification lead at a medical-device manufacturer
**Based on Interviews:** [[P01]], [[P02]], [[P04]], [[P05]], [[P06]], [[P11]]

## Context
Owns or coordinates certification submissions with the notified body, consolidates technical and product data from internal systems and subject-matter experts, and maintains the Appendix ABC evidence needed for active changes and audits. Uses email, meetings, spreadsheets, and internal product-data systems to keep certification work moving.

P05 confirms that this role may manage MDR remediation, Class III maintenance, and renewals across high-volume portfolios, while using direct contact to supplement partial platform visibility.

P06 confirms that Regulatory Affairs leaders own controlled Appendix ABC versions, coordinate data from PLM and other sources, and translate team-level status into management-level reporting.

P11 confirms that Regulatory Affairs teams coordinate open Appendix drafts across product groups, apply approval gates before source-data changes enter certification records, and need user-confirmed rather than autonomous automation.

## Goals
- Submit complete, traceable certification changes without repeated data entry or reconciliation.
- Maintain a reliable current state across internal product data, Appendix ABC, EUDAMED, and notified-body work.
- See request status, timing, and change references without reconstructing them from emails and separate trackers.

notes.title: Make Review Feedback a Traceable Permissioned Workflow

frontmatter.name: Make Review Feedback a Traceable Permissioned Workflow

notes.body:
# Recommendation: Make Review Feedback a Traceable Permissioned Workflow

**Recommendation:** Replace exchanged review-file versions with shared certification records that preserve manufacturer ownership and provide explicit statuses for manufacturer entry, notified-body review, feedback, resolution, and approval. Record field-level changes and comments, restrict status transitions by party so only TUV can set certification authority states, and require customer confirmation before material reviewer-proposed or automated consequential changes become part of the manufacturer-controlled record. Support in-context review comments beside the viewed record rather than requiring a downloaded draft. Link the assessed exemplar to every product record covered by the change and retain the project reference throughout its history.
**Evidence - Anchor Insight:** [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]]
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]], [[Reviewer Feedback Requires Revision Realignment]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce manual comparison and re-entry, prevent loss of reviewer feedback, and make the accountable current state clear to both parties.
**Risk:** The state model and permissions must distinguish material certification changes from low-risk corrections, and scope propagation must not mark unverified records as covered, so the workflow does not introduce false approvals or unnecessary bureaucracy.

## Reference
Each recommendation has exactly one anchor insight; see [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 9.

notes.body:
# Recommendation: Pair Action Alerts with Human Escalation

**Recommendation:** In the certification-status workspace, distinguish action-required deficiencies from routine updates, allow users to mark seen notifications as read without downloading documents, require acknowledgement and escalation for unaddressed actions, and keep a direct project-linked route to the responsible TUV contact. Decouple notification subscriptions from project view and administration rights, and route alerts by project ownership or customer-side responsibility. Use email as an escalation channel for high-priority events, while grouping or suppressing routine change noise through configurable preferences and summaries.
**Evidence - Anchor Insight:** [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]]

notes.body:
# Recommendation: Use Reusable Structured Certification Data

**Recommendation:** Build certificate-specific views from reusable structured product records, beginning with bulk import and prefill from EUDAMED where fields overlap. Support Basic UDI-level reuse so product variants do not require unnecessary article-by-article duplication. Guide users through the remaining certificate-specific fields and offer a documented system-to-system export or integration path for customers with a structured leading system. Preserve the relationships among devices, sites, suppliers, and certification schemes so customers update shared data once rather than maintain parallel Appendix ABC files. Gate synchronization from customer source systems on the appropriate regulatory approval state.
**Evidence - Anchor Insight:** [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]]
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]], [[High-Effort Appendix ABC Maintenance]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce recurring manual updates, duplicate entry, and data inconsistency across certification records.
**Risk:** EUDAMED does not contain every certificate-specific field, some customer source data still live in documents, and mapping quality, transfer timing, access, approval state, and ownership must be validated before treating any source as authoritative.

notes.title: Application and Application Form: Insights and Requirements
notes.body:
# Application and Application Form: Insights and Requirements

## Scope and Evidence Basis

This document consolidates explicit customer statements, needs, pain points, and expectations concerning certification applications, application forms, service requests, change-notification applications, quotation acceptance, and the transition from request to project. It is based on processed interviews P01-P11. Appendix ABC evidence is included only where it is explicitly part of the application or submission workflow.

## Insights and Requirements

### A-01: Customer-Led Application Initiation

**Insight**  
Customers cannot start a certification or significant-change application in the platform before TUV creates a project, so the first step depends on offline contact and setup.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall allow authorized customers to create, classify, save, and submit a new certification or significant-change application before a TUV project exists.

**Description / Background**  
The application journey currently starts outside the platform for customers who need a new project or significant-change record. A customer-led start must create a traceable request that can be handed into TUV project creation without losing its data or history.

**Supporting evidence**  
P10: "UCI nutzen wir. Ja, ist okay. Allerdings muss man ja immer zuerst in U.C.I. muss ja ein Projekt eröffnet werden, bevor man dann irgendwas übermitteln kann, selbst wenn ich jetzt 'ne neue Anfrage hatte, 'ne Significant Change oder so, die kann ich, ich persönlich oder als Kunde kann ich im U.C.I. nicht draufklicken, mach mir was Neues auf und füll das dann da drin an."  
Translation: "We use UCI. It is okay. However, a project must first be opened in UCI before you can submit anything; even when I have a new request or a significant change, I personally, as the customer, cannot click in UCI, create a new item, and complete it there."

**Derived user story**  
As a certification customer, I want to create a new application or significant-change request myself so that I can begin the workflow without waiting for an externally created project.

### A-02: Visible Pre-Application and Project-Creation Status

**Insight**  
The period between a request, quotation or scoping activity, and project creation is opaque. Customers cannot see what happens after they submit or when the request becomes an active project.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall show a request lifecycle from pre-application through project creation, including the current stage, responsible party, next expected action, and handoff outcome.

**Description / Background**  
Participants distinguish between active-project visibility, which can work well, and the earlier phase where a request is assessed, scoped, or converted into a project. The requirement is for transparent workflow state, not a promise of fixed processing time.

**Supporting evidence**  
P09: "Dann ist so 'ne Phase da, die ist für mich quasi schwarz, da weiß ich nicht, was passiert bei Ihnen im Hintergrund."  
Translation: "Then there is a phase that is basically black to me, and I do not know what is happening in the background on your side."

P10: "In der idealen Welt und wir haben das bei Projekten ja auch bei Prozessen bei uns auch so, wenn sie nur in einem System arbeiten mussen, wenn sie das komplett einmal keine PDFs ausfullen mussen, keine irgendwie Antrage machen mussen, also wenn es dann in einem System funktionieren konnte."  
Translation: "In an ideal world, you only have to work in one system and do not have to complete PDFs or separate application forms; it would work in one system."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want to see where my request is between submission and project creation so that I know what is happening and who must act next.

### A-03: Guided, Scenario-Specific Application Forms

**Insight**  
Customers are unsure which documents, fields, and assessment-relevant information are required for different application scenarios. Static forms and generic templates do not provide enough guidance.

**Requirement**  
The application form shall let the customer identify the service or change scenario before committing to a formal request, then display the required fields, documents, definitions, examples, and decision guidance for that scenario.

**Description / Background**  
New-product registrations, product changes, and QMS-related changes have different requirements. Customers want a guided pre-request and application path that reduces repeated clarification and does not rely on a separate wiki or generic template interpretation.

**Supporting evidence**  
P06: "Wenn ich jetzt eine Neuproduktanmeldung habe, was brauchen Sie dafür noch mit dazu, reicht da nur die IFQ, wollen Sie da gleich Broschüren haben oder sonstige Informationen?"  
Translation: "If I have a new product registration, what else do you need for it? Is the IFQ enough, or do you also want brochures or other information?"

P10: "Wenn ich sage, nein, wunscht ihr was, dann habe ich 'ne Plattform, heisst die U.C.I. oder wie auch immer und ich logge mich ein und sage, ich mache 'ne new Application und dann wahle ich aus, will ich jetzt mein Ist es produktbezogen, ist es QM-System bezogen und ich habe eine gewisse Logik dahinter und ich werde dementsprechend durchgefuhrt."  
Translation: "If I could wish for it, I would have a platform where I log in, create a new application, choose whether it concerns a product or the quality-management system, and am guided by the appropriate logic."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want the form to adapt to my application type so that I know exactly what information and evidence I must provide.

### A-04: Contextual Field Guidance and Explainable Validation

**Insight**  
Application and related data-entry fields can be ambiguous, while current validation feedback is unclear. Customers need help at the point of entry and a clear explanation of how to correct a problem.

**Requirement**  
The application form shall provide inline field guidance, controlled value selection where applicable, validation before submission, and error messages that identify the affected field and corrective action.

**Description / Background**  
Participants describe asking experts what a field requires, encountering cryptic validation output, and wanting information icons and linked guidance. Formal checks should help the customer identify issues; they should not silently change the application.

**Supporting evidence**  
P08: "Dann kommt es ganz oft mit Hashtag Wert Ausrufezeichen und wir wissen halt auch nicht, was haben wir jetzt da falsch gemacht oder ist da jetzt, also es verunsichert halt einfach 'n bisschen."  
Translation: "It often then shows hashtag value exclamation mark, and we do not know what we have done wrong; it is simply a bit unsettling."

P11: "Wenn ich jetzt bei einem den Eintrag eher fuge einen E. R. C. Code fur diese Seite hinzu und wenn da jetzt ein Icon ware, Information, Achtung, ERC Codes, blablabla, einfach so ein bisschen und ein paar Links, ja klar, ware naturlich immer toll."  
Translation: "If I add an ERC code for a site, it would be helpful to have an information icon with guidance and links about ERC codes."

**Derived user story**  
As an application-form user, I want field-level guidance and understandable validation feedback so that I can correct an issue before submitting the form.

### A-05: Staged Application Data and Controlled Amendments

**Insight**  
Some product, supplier, and impact-assessment details are legitimately unavailable or still evolving when an application is first submitted. Forcing final data too early causes resubmission and duplicate work.

**Requirement**  
The application workflow shall support staged data capture, clearly distinguish pending from submitted information, and allow controlled amendments that preserve the original submission and its later updates. A source-data change shall not update a submitted or approved certification record until the applicable regulatory approval state permits it; consequential related-record changes must require accountable user confirmation.

**Description / Background**  
A change notification may precede final technical details. Participants also report discovering incomplete impact assessment after submission. The workflow must make missing or later-required information visible without treating a changed source record as automatically approved certification data.

**Supporting evidence**  
P07: "Oft ist es ja so, dass wenn man 'ne Change Notification einreicht, dass zu dem Zeitpunkt die Details, die in den Appendix eingetragen werden mussen, noch nicht klar sind, auch noch nicht vonnoten sind."  
Translation: "When submitting a change notification, the details that must be entered in the Appendix are often not yet clear or needed at that time."

P03: "If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want to submit the information that is required and available now, then provide controlled amendments when later-stage details are ready, so that I avoid rebuilding the application.

### A-06: Compliant Digital Authorization and Acceptance

**Insight**  
Signed and write-protected quotation or application documents force local PDF editing, print-and-scan, and re-upload work. Customers want a digital authorization step that does not prevent required customer information from being completed.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall support a role-controlled digital authorization or signature workflow for application and quotation acceptance, including required customer reference fields, without requiring users to modify a locked PDF locally.

**Description / Background**  
The requirement is not to remove necessary authorization. It is to replace the current workaround in which a signed document cannot accept required information and must be recreated or processed outside the platform.

**Supporting evidence**  
P10: "Das kann ich aber nicht eintragen, weil das PDF digital signiert ist vom TUV. Das kann ich nicht andern. Das kann ich aber auch nicht als PDF drucken. Das muss ich ausdrucken und scannen."  
Translation: "I cannot enter that because the PDF is digitally signed by TUV. I cannot change it, nor can I print it as a PDF. I have to print and scan it."

P11: "Eure Quotation ist unterschrieben und schreibgeschutzt. Ich muss mir die runterladen, dann druck ich mir die noch mal ins PDF, damit die nicht mehr schreibgeschutzt ist."  
Translation: "Your quotation is signed and write-protected. I have to download it and print it again as a PDF so that it is no longer write-protected."

**Derived user story**  
As an authorized customer representative, I want to provide the required approval and reference information digitally so that I can accept an application or quotation without a print-and-scan workaround.

### A-07: Link One Submission to All Relevant Projects and Scope

**Insight**  
The same application evidence is copied into several change-notification and general projects, while a submitted exemplar may represent many products that must later be updated manually.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall allow one application submission or evidence record to be linked to all relevant projects, change notifications, and in-scope products while retaining project-specific identifiers and status. It shall retain the relationship between an assessed exemplar and the full affected scope, then support a guided, approval-controlled bulk update of related records after the assessment outcome.

**Description / Background**  
Customers currently duplicate the same file, rename it with several change-notification references, and upload it to multiple locations. They also submit an exemplar for assessment while maintaining many additional affected products afterward. A linked-submission model must make these relationships explicit without assuming that every project or in-scope record shares the same approval state.

**Supporting evidence**  
P11: "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen."  
Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

P09: "Wir mussen aber immer im Hinterkopf behalten, wir haben da noch 100 andere Artikel, die auch uber diesen selben Vorgang laufen, die haben wir aber nicht eingereicht, die mussen aber dann im Nachgang auch alle noch gepflegt werden."  
Translation: "We must always remember that another 100 articles run through the same change; we did not submit them, but they all still have to be maintained afterward."

**Derived user story**  
As a Regulatory Affairs user, I want to link one application and its evidence to every relevant project and affected product, then apply the approved assessment outcome to the identified scope in a controlled bulk action so that I do not copy files or manually reconstruct the scope.

### A-08: Immutable Submission Receipt and Review Status

**Insight**  
Customers cannot reliably verify when a request was submitted, whether TUV has received or reviewed it, or whether a response is currently expected.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall record an immutable submission timestamp and show receipt, opened, reviewed, and response-required states for each application or request.

**Description / Background**  
A "last edited" date is not proof of submission. Participants request acknowledgement that their information has been received or reviewed, particularly when no immediate response is needed.

**Supporting evidence**  
P09: "Das hab ich auch schon mal angemerkt, dass man da nicht sehen kann, wann der Service Request wirklich ubermittelt wurde. Ich glaub, da steht nur 'zuletzt bearbeitet' Stand oder sowas wird angezeigt."  
Translation: "I have already pointed out that you cannot see when the service request was actually submitted. I think it only shows a 'last edited' status or something similar."

P06: "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TUV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grune Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen."  
Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want an immutable submission receipt and review status so that I can confirm the request was transmitted and know whether I need to act.

### A-09: Preserve Application Documents Through Project Handoff

**Insight**  
Application forms and supporting documents disappear from the customer-visible record once a request becomes a project, breaking traceability of what was originally requested.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall retain submitted application forms, checklists, supporting documents, customer references, and submission history as read-only, project-linked records throughout the project lifecycle. Where issued for the project, final certificates and assessment reports shall remain linked and accessible in the same customer-visible record.

**Description / Background**  
Original application materials are required to understand the requested scope and enable newly authorized project stakeholders to see what was submitted. The handoff must preserve the original record rather than create an isolated project view.

**Supporting evidence**  
P08: "Wenn das Projekt angelegt wurde, ich sehe die Antragsunterlagen nicht mehr in U.C.I."  
Translation: "When the project has been created, I can no longer see the application documents in UCI."

P09: "Wenn ich im kompletten Projekt alles drin hab, dass auch jemand, den ich aufs Projekt zugreifen lasse, auch dann die ganzen Application Form sehen kann, was wir beantragt haben."  
Translation: "When everything is in the complete project, someone whom I give project access should also be able to see all the application forms showing what we requested."

P09: "Es würde uns sehr helfen, wenn die Zertifikate und die finalen Assessment Reports in UCI hochgeladen werden."  
Translation: "It would help us greatly if the certificates and final assessment reports were uploaded in UCI."

**Derived user story**  
As a project stakeholder, I want to retrieve the original application and its evidence from the active project so that I can see exactly what was requested and submitted.

### A-10: Keep Application Follow-Up in Context

**Insight**  
Customers must leave the request record and reconstruct the request number and date in email to send a reminder or ask a follow-up question.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall provide request-linked messages, reminders, and follow-up actions that retain the application reference, submitted documents, current status, and conversation history.

**Description / Background**  
Email is used as a workaround when the request cannot be reopened or discussed in context. This divides the application history across systems and increases administrative effort.

**Supporting evidence**  
P02: "Ich kann den Request nicht aufgreifen. Das heisst, ich muss auf das E-Mail zuruckkommen, um den Request mit der Nummer zum Gluck dann aufzugreifen und auch das Datum nochmals aufzugreifen, um das zu reminden."  
Translation: "I cannot pick up the request again. That means I have to return to email to pick up the request with its number and date again in order to send a reminder."

P03: "Most of the communication are managed via mail. And sometimes it's easy to lost the mail and lost the traceability."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want to follow up from the original request record so that I do not have to reconstruct the request context in email.

### A-11: Explain Commercial Scope Before Authorization

**Insight**  
Customers may understand which certification service they need, but cannot reliably understand the cost components or assessment-module rationale before accepting a quotation.

**Requirement**  
The application or quotation workflow shall display the proposed assessment modules, cost components, relevant assumptions, and rationale before the authorized customer accepts the quotation.

**Description / Background**  
This is a commercial-scoping requirement, not a request to expose internal decision making. Customers need enough explanation to forecast the cost, understand the proposed scope, and raise a traceable question before authorization.

**Supporting evidence**  
P02: "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg."  
Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

P07: "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhohung, konnt ihr uns das bitte erklaren?"  
Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

**Derived user story**  
As an authorized customer representative, I want to understand the modules and costs in a quotation before accepting it so that I can make an informed commitment.

### A-12: Show Action Ownership and Use Focused Application Alerts

**Insight**  
During application assessment, customers cannot always tell whether the next action belongs to them or TUV. Broad notification streams also make important actions easy to overlook.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall show the current action owner, due date, and next milestone for each application or project, and provide configurable, task-specific alerts that are independent of general project-access rights.

**Description / Background**  
Customers value notification of a specific deadline or required action, but do not want alert volume generated merely by administrator or visibility permissions. The workflow must make ownership and deadlines actionable without adding noise.

**Supporting evidence**  
P10: "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. furs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prufung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prufung, das ist O.K. Ich wusste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen konnte in der Ubersicht. Das ware ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TUV. Das sieht man primar nicht."  
Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; Dornier owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."

P09: "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich uberhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss."  
Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

**Derived user story**  
As an application stakeholder, I want to see who owns the next action and receive only relevant reminders so that I respond on time without searching through unrelated notifications.

## Evidence Constraints

- Customers accept digitalization when it preserves required authorization, controlled approval, and data accountability.
- A changed source record must not automatically become an approved certification or application record; consequential changes require the appropriate regulatory control and user confirmation.
- Customers value focused, task-specific reminders and do not want high-volume general project notifications.
- The initial request, project handoff, and active project should form one traceable record, but the evidence does not require a fixed TUV response-time commitment.
- Guided self-service must retain a clear path to named human guidance or escalation when an application case remains ambiguous.
- The application workflow should preserve a centralized active-project workspace rather than dispersing customer-visible records across separate systems.

Translation: "It often then shows hashtag value exclamation mark, and we do not know what we have done wrong; it is simply a bit unsettling."

P11: "Wenn ich jetzt bei einem den Eintrag eher fuge einen E. R. C. Code fur diese Seite hinzu und wenn da jetzt ein Icon ware, Information, Achtung, ERC Codes, blablabla, einfach so ein bisschen und ein paar Links, ja klar, ware naturlich immer toll."  
Translation: "If I add an ERC code for a site, it would be helpful to have an information icon with guidance and links about ERC codes."

**Derived user story**  
As an application-form user, I want field-level guidance and understandable validation feedback so that I can correct an issue before submitting the form.

### A-05: Staged Application Data and Controlled Amendments

**Insight**  
Some product, supplier, and impact-assessment details are legitimately unavailable or still evolving when an application is first submitted. Forcing final data too early causes resubmission and duplicate work.

**Requirement**  
The application workflow shall support staged data capture, clearly distinguish pending from submitted information, and allow controlled amendments that preserve the original submission and its later updates. A source-data change shall not update a submitted or approved certification record until the applicable regulatory approval state permits it; consequential related-record changes must require accountable user confirmation.

**Description / Background**  
A change notification may precede final technical details. Participants also report discovering incomplete impact assessment after submission. The workflow must make missing or later-required information visible without treating a changed source record as automatically approved certification data.

**Supporting evidence**  
P07: "Oft ist es ja so, dass wenn man 'ne Change Notification einreicht, dass zu dem Zeitpunkt die Details, die in den Appendix eingetragen werden mussen, noch nicht klar sind, auch noch nicht vonnoten sind."  
Translation: "When submitting a change notification, the details that must be entered in the Appendix are often not yet clear or needed at that time."

P03: "If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want to submit the information that is required and available now, then provide controlled amendments when later-stage details are ready, so that I avoid rebuilding the application.

### A-06: Compliant Digital Authorization and Acceptance

**Insight**  
Signed and write-protected quotation or application documents force local PDF editing, print-and-scan, and re-upload work. Customers want a digital authorization step that does not prevent required customer information from being completed.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall support a role-controlled digital authorization or signature workflow for application and quotation acceptance, including required customer reference fields, without requiring users to modify a locked PDF locally.

**Description / Background**  
The requirement is not to remove necessary authorization. It is to replace the current workaround in which a signed document cannot accept required information and must be recreated or processed outside the platform.

**Supporting evidence**  
P10: "Das kann ich aber nicht eintragen, weil das PDF digital signiert ist vom TUV. Das kann ich nicht andern. Das kann ich aber auch nicht als PDF drucken. Das muss ich ausdrucken und scannen."  
Translation: "I cannot enter that because the PDF is digitally signed by TUV. I cannot change it, nor can I print it as a PDF. I have to print and scan it."

P11: "Eure Quotation ist unterschrieben und schreibgeschutzt. Ich muss mir die runterladen, dann druck ich mir die noch mal ins PDF, damit die nicht mehr schreibgeschutzt ist."  
Translation: "Your quotation is signed and write-protected. I have to download it and print it again as a PDF so that it is no longer write-protected."

**Derived user story**  
As an authorized customer representative, I want to provide the required approval and reference information digitally so that I can accept an application or quotation without a print-and-scan workaround.

### A-07: Link One Submission to All Relevant Projects and Scope

**Insight**  
The same application evidence is copied into several change-notification and general projects, while a submitted exemplar may represent many products that must later be updated manually.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall allow one application submission or evidence record to be linked to all relevant projects, change notifications, and in-scope products while retaining project-specific identifiers and status. It shall retain the relationship between an assessed exemplar and the full affected scope, then support a guided, approval-controlled bulk update of related records after the assessment outcome.

**Description / Background**  
Customers currently duplicate the same file, rename it with several change-notification references, and upload it to multiple locations. They also submit an exemplar for assessment while maintaining many additional affected products afterward. A linked-submission model must make these relationships explicit without assuming that every project or in-scope record shares the same approval state.

**Supporting evidence**  
P11: "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen."  
Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

P09: "Wir mussen aber immer im Hinterkopf behalten, wir haben da noch 100 andere Artikel, die auch uber diesen selben Vorgang laufen, die haben wir aber nicht eingereicht, die mussen aber dann im Nachgang auch alle noch gepflegt werden."  
Translation: "We must always remember that another 100 articles run through the same change; we did not submit them, but they all still have to be maintained afterward."

**Derived user story**  
As a Regulatory Affairs user, I want to link one application and its evidence to every relevant project and affected product, then apply the approved assessment outcome to the identified scope in a controlled bulk action so that I do not copy files or manually reconstruct the scope.

### A-08: Immutable Submission Receipt and Review Status

**Insight**  
Customers cannot reliably verify when a request was submitted, whether TUV has received or reviewed it, or whether a response is currently expected.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall record an immutable submission timestamp and show receipt, opened, reviewed, and response-required states for each application or request.

**Description / Background**  
A "last edited" date is not proof of submission. Participants request acknowledgement that their information has been received or reviewed, particularly when no immediate response is needed.

**Supporting evidence**  
P09: "Das hab ich auch schon mal angemerkt, dass man da nicht sehen kann, wann der Service Request wirklich ubermittelt wurde. Ich glaub, da steht nur 'zuletzt bearbeitet' Stand oder sowas wird angezeigt."  
Translation: "I have already pointed out that you cannot see when the service request was actually submitted. I think it only shows a 'last edited' status or something similar."

P06: "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TUV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grune Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen."  
Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want an immutable submission receipt and review status so that I can confirm the request was transmitted and know whether I need to act.

### A-09: Preserve Application Documents Through Project Handoff

**Insight**  
Application forms and supporting documents disappear from the customer-visible record once a request becomes a project, breaking traceability of what was originally requested.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall retain submitted application forms, checklists, supporting documents, customer references, and submission history as read-only, project-linked records throughout the project lifecycle. Where issued for the project, final certificates and assessment reports shall remain linked and accessible in the same customer-visible record.

**Description / Background**  
Original application materials are required to understand the requested scope and enable newly authorized project stakeholders to see what was submitted. The handoff must preserve the original record rather than create an isolated project view.

**Supporting evidence**  
P08: "Wenn das Projekt angelegt wurde, ich sehe die Antragsunterlagen nicht mehr in U.C.I."  
Translation: "When the project has been created, I can no longer see the application documents in UCI."

P09: "Wenn ich im kompletten Projekt alles drin hab, dass auch jemand, den ich aufs Projekt zugreifen lasse, auch dann die ganzen Application Form sehen kann, was wir beantragt haben."  
Translation: "When everything is in the complete project, someone whom I give project access should also be able to see all the application forms showing what we requested."

P09: "Es würde uns sehr helfen, wenn die Zertifikate und die finalen Assessment Reports in UCI hochgeladen werden."  
Translation: "It would help us greatly if the certificates and final assessment reports were uploaded in UCI."

**Derived user story**  
As a project stakeholder, I want to retrieve the original application and its evidence from the active project so that I can see exactly what was requested and submitted.

### A-10: Keep Application Follow-Up in Context

**Insight**  
Customers must leave the request record and reconstruct the request number and date in email to send a reminder or ask a follow-up question.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall provide request-linked messages, reminders, and follow-up actions that retain the application reference, submitted documents, current status, and conversation history.

**Description / Background**  
Email is used as a workaround when the request cannot be reopened or discussed in context. This divides the application history across systems and increases administrative effort.

**Supporting evidence**  
P02: "Ich kann den Request nicht aufgreifen. Das heisst, ich muss auf das E-Mail zuruckkommen, um den Request mit der Nummer zum Gluck dann aufzugreifen und auch das Datum nochmals aufzugreifen, um das zu reminden."  
Translation: "I cannot pick up the request again. That means I have to return to email to pick up the request with its number and date again in order to send a reminder."

P03: "Most of the communication are managed via mail. And sometimes it's easy to lost the mail and lost the traceability."

**Derived user story**  
As an applicant, I want to follow up from the original request record so that I do not have to reconstruct the request context in email.

### A-11: Explain Commercial Scope Before Authorization

**Insight**  
Customers may understand which certification service they need, but cannot reliably understand the cost components or assessment-module rationale before accepting a quotation.

**Requirement**  
The application or quotation workflow shall display the proposed assessment modules, cost components, relevant assumptions, and rationale before the authorized customer accepts the quotation.

**Description / Background**  
This is a commercial-scoping requirement, not a request to expose internal decision making. Customers need enough explanation to forecast the cost, understand the proposed scope, and raise a traceable question before authorization.

**Supporting evidence**  
P02: "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg."  
Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

P07: "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhohung, konnt ihr uns das bitte erklaren?"  
Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

**Derived user story**  
As an authorized customer representative, I want to understand the modules and costs in a quotation before accepting it so that I can make an informed commitment.

### A-12: Show Action Ownership and Use Focused Application Alerts

**Insight**  
During application assessment, customers cannot always tell whether the next action belongs to them or TUV. Broad notification streams also make important actions easy to overlook.

**Requirement**  
The platform shall show the current action owner, due date, and next milestone for each application or project, and provide configurable, task-specific alerts that are independent of general project-access rights.

**Description / Background**  
Customers value notification of a specific deadline or required action, but do not want alert volume generated merely by administrator or visibility permissions. The workflow must make ownership and deadlines actionable without adding noise.

**Supporting evidence**  
P10: "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. furs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prufung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prufung, das ist O.K. Ich wusste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen konnte in der Ubersicht. Das ware ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TUV. Das sieht man primar nicht."  
Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; Dornier owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."

P09: "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich uberhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss."  
Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

**Derived user story**  
As an application stakeholder, I want to see who owns the next action and receive only relevant reminders so that I respond on time without searching through unrelated notifications.
sections.Evidence Constraints:
- Customers accept digitalization when it preserves required authorization, controlled approval, and data accountability.
- A changed source record must not automatically become an approved certification or application record; consequential changes require the appropriate regulatory control and user confirmation.
- Customers value focused, task-specific reminders and do not want high-volume general project notifications.
- The initial request, project handoff, and active project should form one traceable record, but the evidence does not require a fixed TUV response-time commitment.
- Guided self-service must retain a clear path to named human guidance or escalation when an application case remains ambiguous.
- The application workflow should preserve a centralized active-project workspace rather than dispersing customer-visible records across separate systems.

fields.Insight: Customers cannot start a certification or significant-change application in the platform before TUV creates a project, so the first step depends on offline contact and setup.
fields.Requirement: The platform shall allow authorized customers to create, classify, save, and submit a new certification or significant-change application before a TUV project exists.
fields.Description / Background: The application journey currently starts outside the platform for customers who need a new project or significant-change record. A customer-led start must create a traceable request that can be handed into TUV project creation without losing its data or history.

Allerdings muss man ja immer zuerst in U.C.I. muss ja ein Projekt eröffnet werden, bevor man dann irgendwas übermitteln kann, selbst wenn ich jetzt 'ne neue Anfrage hatte, 'ne Significant Change oder so, die kann ich, ich persönlich oder als Kunde kann ich im U.C.I. nicht draufklicken, mach mir was Neues auf und füll das dann da drin an."
